# Lifecycle of a work item > Part of the burhan working agreement (core:
you take in a request, write a story or a plan, or the approved intent changes.
## The lifecycle of one work item Work one item at a time, end to end, unless told otherwise.
Order dependent items so that whoever produces data comes before whoever consumes it.

② STORY (S) templates/story.md — job story, acceptance criteria with IDs and provenance (copied from the source of truth, not paraphrased), business rules, open questions, codebase verification (file:line), proposed sub-units.
Too big for one plan → propose a split (below).

③ PLAN (P) templates/plan.md and templates/build-spec.md — re-verify the story's facts against the CURRENT code (what the story got wrong, with file:line), options + recommendation, rulings, the AC → test coverage, the executor rules; the build spec holds, per sub-unit, the files, the complete test, the RED and GREEN commands with their expected output, the complete code and the interfaces.
A template placeholder left in the story, the plan or the build spec blocks it too (approve names it).
④ BUILD (T) Re-validate the plan against current code before the first sub-unit.
failing test → smallest change → green → fast check.

After each sub-unit run the tests that relate to the part you changed, which you pick from the diff and name with the reason, then the fast check; never the whole suite by default (a large project's suite can take hours:
record it in the plan's Deviations table (burhan deviation add), ask the owner, and only an approved deviation changes the plan and spec first, then the code.
A plan that no longer matches the code is worse than none — update it.
⑤ REVIEW (R) Independent review of each sub-unit's diff (phases/review.md) → a section in reviews/<slug>-review.md (short or full, by risk).
⑥ VERIFY (V) Real end-to-end check as the verification identity.
every AC → satisfied / partial / missing / contradicts, plus unrequested behaviour.
→ reviews/<slug>-qc.md · PASS / FAIL Run in a fresh context (core principle 8).
⑧ KNOWLEDGE (K) Propose durable learnings → promote / reject, or record "none" (phases/memory.md).
✅ CLOSE-OUT Only after the gates the route requires.
Definition of done = every gate the route requires is ticked in the plan's Gate checklist.
A happy-path check is the most common way defects reach QA — that is why ⑥ and ⑦ exist.

## Read-only work Read-only work (investigation, bug + spike).
Question → evidence → findings → limitations → conclusion.
the work item's own docs, discovery files and the state file may still be written.
When the human asks for a fully read-only pass, write nothing at all and report what would be recorded.
To implement a finding, open a new routed item.
## Working methods exploration → specification → test-first implementation → systematic debugging → review → verification.
## The patch lane For one obvious change (core §3 · patch).
The state file records it as a Now entry ### <slug> with - Route:
<type> / patch — or not at all when it is committed in the same turn.
A patch that grows (an escalator, a sensitive path, a second concern, any doubt) is promoted to bounded at once, and the promotion is said out loud in the reply.
## Re-validation by diff The story's Codebase verification records Verified at commit (the sha at which its facts were checked).
Before the plan, and again before the first sub-unit, run burhan changed --item <slug>:
re-check only the facts whose files it lists, and write the list — or "no change since <sha>" — in the plan.
No sha, or a sha that is not a commit here → re-check every fact.
## Modes — where the flow stops for the human A mode is a gate in burhan's flow, not the agent's permission mode — the vendor's permission or approval settings stay whatever the human chose.

| Mode | In plain words | Stops at | |---|---|---| | step (default) | "wait for my approval" | story · plan · after every sub-unit · commit | | auto | "carry on on your own" | story and plan once (one gate on bounded routes) · brakes · commit | The route sets how many stops the item has, by its risk — not the mode; the mode only decides whether the build pauses between sub-units.
Plan only is a stopping point, not a mode:
when the human asks for the plan only, stop after the plan is approved, close the item at Plan ready, and write no code.
- Ask for the mode at the start of each item (the default comes from WF_MODE_<TYPE>_<SCOPE>, else WF_MODE_DEFAULT, else step); record it as Mode in the story and the state file's Now.
- The human switches it any time in plain words ("go end to end" / "كمّل لوحدك" → auto; "wait for my approval" / "استنى موافقتي" → step); write the switch to the state file.
- Brakes — auto falls back to asking when:
a scope escalator appears mid-work · an out-of-scope discovery · the plan must change · the same test fails twice in a row · an irreversible action.
- The commit checkpoint always stops, in every mode.
"Who verifies?" is asked once, at the start, in auto.
## Decision card — the first lines of a story and a plan The first lines of <slug>-story.md and <slug>-implementation-plan.md, down to the first blank line, are a decision card:
what changes, the files it touches, the risks, the route, and the decisions needed from the human.
Present the card at the ⛔ STOP; approval is given on the card — the rest of the file is the evidence behind it, read only when the human wants to.
## Questions — one round Ask all open questions together, once, as a numbered list (Q-1, Q-2, …) in the story — never trickle them across turns.
An answer that changes scope is an intent change (below).
## When the intent changes mid-flight If the approved intent changes (new source, changed AC, answered question that alters scope) after the story was approved:
record an impact entry in the plan's Impact log — for each completed phase, affected or unaffected with a reason — then revise only the affected phases.
Evidence is never deleted; superseded results are marked, not erased.
Convergence findings on changed AC are stale and must be re-assessed.
## Decomposition An item too large for one plan becomes a parent with children, each its own folder and route.
Each child lists the parent's AC IDs it answers for and its depends on siblings.
The parent is done only when every required child is done.
a child reaching done is reported as "child X done, N/M children complete" — never as "project done".
## Readiness is not stage An item may legitimately stop before implementation:
Spec ready (story approved, nothing planned), Plan ready (plan approved, nothing built).
